findings.location: scripts/run_events.py derive_log (GATE -> VERIFICATION subjectSpanId; HOOK as a point), _run_scope; README 'Derivation from the agent loop' (Precondition)
findings.finding: MAS-RA-008 lets a GATE name any earlier step as its subject (_references: v.before), a HOOK step included. derive_log turns a HOOK step into a point on the run span but still sets the VERIFICATION's subjectSpanId to span_id_for(run, hookStepId), a span that never starts. P30: agent-loop V021 plus a passing unit-tests GATE whose subject is the HOOK step 'audit' (tokens and wall-clock 0, totals unchanged) passes MAS-RA-008's check_trace; its derived log is refused RUN_SCOPE (with RUN_SCOPE disabled it passes, and to_otel raises KeyError on it). So a log naming that trace is refused RUN_SCOPE, not DERIVATION. The README and derive_log's docstring state one precondition only, distinct trace ids (R1-3); the statement that derive_log turns a trace passing its own check into its log, apart from that precondition, does not hold. The 36 vector traces are unaffected (none gates a hook; P50). For the record, P70: a trace under a profile whose wall-clock budget allows a step of 10^13 s also passes MAS-RA-008, and its derived log has timeMs above 2^53 - 1 and is refused SHAPE.
findings.requiredChange: Derive a gate on a HOOK step faithfully (for example a HOOK as a zero-length span, or a subject rule that accepts the point), or state the second precondition (a gate's subject is a MODEL, TOOL, GATE or DELEGATE step; derived times within 2^53 - 1 ms) in derive_log and the README and refuse it in derive_log as DERIVATION, with a vector.

findings.location: scripts/run_events.py _run_scope (subjectSpanId, revisesSpanId); compute_metrics (evidence_coverage, verifier_disagreement); README Rules (RUN_SCOPE)
findings.finding: A verification's subject and a revision's target need only have started earlier in the same run. Nothing requires them to have ended, so a verdict can be recorded on bytes that do not exist yet. P32: the team log's root schema-check verification of the merge span moved to 4400-4450 ms with outcome OK, inside the merge span (which ends at 5000 ms and only then produces F), is accepted, and evidence_coverage goes from 4/7 to 5/7. P31: w1's unit-tests verification runs 1100-1200 ms and ends before the draft it verifies ends (3000 ms): accepted. P33: a verification naming its own open RUN span as subject: accepted (its OK covers the run's delivered bytes, and the evaluation event lands on the invoke_agent span). P34: a revision nested inside the span it revises: accepted. Coverage and disagreement read the subject's END outputHash, so they trust an order the log does not guarantee. Every derived log already satisfies the stricter order: across the 36 derived logs, 0 verifications start before their subject ends and 0 revisions before their target ends (P51). The team log satisfies it too.
findings.requiredChange: Require the subject span and the revised span to have ended before the verification or the revision starts (its END earlier in sequence and no later in time), with a refusal vector. Otherwise, state in Not claimed that evidence coverage and verifier disagreement trust the recorded order.

findings.location: scripts/run_events.py (no rule binds an AGENT_INVOKE END to its child RUN END); compute_metrics evidence_coverage; to_otel (delegate span status)
findings.finding: A delegation's END is not bound to its child run's END. P36: in the team log, invoke-2 ends OK with output X (and a payloadRef to it) while its child w2-run ends FAILED with no output. The log is accepted. evidence_coverage moves from 4/7 to 5/8, because the delegation now counts as a covered OK output, and the projected delegate span loses its ERROR status. P37: invoke-1 END with tokens 99 against its child's 2000: accepted. MAS-RA-008 binds exactly these (TOTALS_MISMATCH: a DELEGATE step is OK exactly when its child COMPLETED, its artefact is the child's delivered artefact, and its tokens and wall-clock are the child's). So every derived log satisfies the binding, and the hand-written team log does too. The README's 'A record, not a monitor' covers whether tokens are true, not whether two events of one log agree; MESSAGE_PAIRING checks that kind of agreement for messages.
findings.requiredChange: Add the binding to RUN_SCOPE or a new rule, with a refusal vector: the AGENT_INVOKE END is OK exactly when the child RUN END is COMPLETED, with the same outputHash and payloadRef and the same tokens. Otherwise, state in Not claimed that a delegation's outcome, output and tokens are not checked against its child run.

findings.location: scripts/run_events.py _time_order, _message_pairing; README rules TIME_ORDER and MESSAGE_PAIRING
findings.finding: A message can be received earlier in time than it was sent. P35: the orchestrator's RECEIVE of m2 at 1000 ms against w1's SEND at 3200 ms, with the logical order kept, is accepted (round 1's P07 gave the same result). TIME_ORDER treats timeMs as one clock, milliseconds from the root run's start, and nests every span in it. On that clock, a receive before its send is not a causal order. Derived logs hold no messages.
findings.requiredChange: Require a receive's timeMs to be no earlier than its send's, or state in the README that message times may be skewed between agents and only logical time orders a message.

findings.location: README 'Derivation from the agent loop' (What a derived log leaves to the trace), 'The run-event log' (attributes), OTel bullet on points
findings.finding: (1) The list of what a derived log leaves to the trace omits the following: the loop profile digest; the terminal reason (P63: derived V024, HOOK_ABORT, and V025, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, both end ABORTED with no reason); the errorTraceDigest of non-gate steps (only a gate's goes to outputHash); a tool call's timeout, limits and sandbox-profile digest ('budgets' may be meant to cover some of these); and the child trace digests of DELEGATE steps. (2) The README says tokens are inclusive (a run's tokens include its delegations'), but it does not say whether a run's costMicros is. The team log's root cost is 60 against child costs of 20 and 17, and cost_per_success reads only root costs. (3) 'Points become span events named planeon.<operation>': the names are lower-cased (planeon.message).
findings.requiredChange: Complete the list, or carry the terminal reason. State whether a run's costMicros includes its delegations'. Say that the event names are lower-case.

findings.location: scripts/run_events.py to_otel (status, error.type); README OTel mapping, first bullet
findings.finding: Every END outcome other than OK or COMPLETED sets span status ERROR and error.type. A gate's FAIL or UNKNOWN verdict therefore makes its verify span an error (team projection: 'verify unit-tests' ERROR FAIL, 'verify schema-check' ERROR UNKNOWN), and a HANDED_OFF run (derived V022) becomes an error span (P62). OTel's error status and the pinned error.type describe an operation that failed. A gate that ran and returned FAIL, and a designed hand-off to a human, did not fail as operations, so error-rate views will count verdicts and hand-offs as errors. The rule is stated in the README, so this is a reading note.
findings.requiredChange: Optionally limit ERROR status to outcomes that are operation errors and carry verdicts in the evaluation event, or state in the README that verdicts and hand-offs count as errors in OTel views.

dispositions.evidence: derive_log(trace, stores, loop, bindings) takes runManifestDigest, verdictLedgerDigest and costMicros, and DERIVATION derives with bindings_of(doc). The new SOURCE_BINDING rule binds manifest.runId to rootRunId and manifest.ledgerDigest to the log's ledger (vector R035; P04 a ledger named against a manifest whose ledgerDigest is null: SOURCE_BINDING). The cost is costMicros (unit cost-micros/success). Valid R012, a derived log bound to a manifest that passes MAS-RA-002's check_manifest in the builder, passes (P01). R013 has cost_per_success 125000/1 DEFINED (P06). Changing the root cost is accepted as a binding (P02). A child RUN END cost is refused DERIVATION (P05). A manifest under a key that is not its digest is refused UNKNOWN_REFERENCE (P07). The README states the runId binding.

MODEL_CALL START carries provider and model (nullable identifiers), and no exporterSupplied entry remains (grep: 0 in the model and vectors). The README states that a log without the provider (every derived log) projects a chat span without the required gen_ai.provider.name. P09: 0 of the chat spans of derived V020 carry it. My own parse of spans.yaml shows that gen_ai.provider.name is the only required gen_ai attribute of gen_ai.client.inference, and it is mapped.

derive_log refuses a repeated trace id in a delegation tree as DERIVATION (seen_runs). Vector R036 (child reuses the parent's id) gives DERIVATION. P11 (V046's second child reuses the first child's id; MAS-RA-008 PASS) gives DERIVATION. 36 of 36 valid agent-loop traces derive and pass, byte-identical under reversed member order (P50). A further unstated precondition, a gate on a hook step, is new finding R2-1.

Every pattern in the three schemas ends in (?![\s\S]), including the lookaheads inside the all-zero span and trace ids. The builder runs a newline sweep (480 strings). My own sweep (P71) ran 11,745 single-leaf mutations: 2 disagreements, both the documented schemaAccepts evidence order, and 0 non-Refused exceptions.
RUN_SCOPE requires each event's agentId to be its run's RUN START agentId (vector R026). Round 1's P06 (w1's receive recorded in orch-run) is now RUN_SCOPE (P12), and so is the 'ghost' claim (P13).

TIME_ORDER now nests times: the root starts at 0 ms, a span ends within its parent, and a point lies within its span (vectors R029, R030, R031). Round 1's P03 (root END at 100 ms; P14) and P02 (worker END at 9000 ms; P15), and a point after its run's END (P16), are refused TIME_ORDER. derive_log stretches run and delegation ENDs to their latest content (latest()), and all 36 derived logs pass.

_stored applies content addressing to sources, report logs and annotated logs, and annotated logs are checked (ANNOTATION_INPUT; vectors R039 and R047, P21). Round 1's P17, P18 and P14 are now UNKNOWN_REFERENCE (P17, P18, P19). An arbitrary value stored under its own digest as a manifest is SOURCE_BINDING (P20). The README states that manifests and ledgers are checked for presence, digest and binding only.

HOOK points carry result and tokens, and VERIFICATION END and HANDOFF carry tokens. P22: derived V050 shows result ERROR and passes. P23: in all 45 runs of the 36 derived logs, RUN END tokens equal the sum of the run's own END and point tokens. The README lists what a derived log leaves to the trace; the list is incomplete (NOTE R2-5).

Disagreement is keyed by (gateId, subject bytes, or the subject span when it has no output). Coverage is keyed by bytes over model calls, untrusted tool results and delegations. P24: derived V042, V032, V044, V046 and V020 are all 1/1 (round 1: 1/4, 2/3, 3/5). The team values (verifier_disagreement 1/3, evidence_coverage 4/7) match my independent recomputation. Annotation a2 now cites the same gate (unit-tests) on the same bytes with OK (w1) and FAIL (w2), which is what the metric counts.

P26: the pinned projections have 0 null attribute values and 0 invoke_agent spans directly under an invoke_agent span. Span names are chat, chat team-model, delegate, execute_tool write-file, invoke_agent, verify schema-check and verify unit-tests, with no run or agent ids. P27: evaluation events sit only on the evaluated (subject) spans. The delegate span carries no tokens, and the README states that planeon.tokens is inclusive and never summed.
The 'Expressiveness' bullet in Not claimed states all four limits: external A2A peers, no broadcast, claims never released (a hand-over counts in conflicting_claim_rate), and depth at most 1.
